problem: Prior AI2-THOR object-goal navigation agents (SAVN, ORG) encode observations by concatenating features or by building a graph from one highest-confidence detection per class. They discard other instances of the same class, are hurt by false positives, use scale-sensitive Faster R-CNN backbone features, and do not tie image-region position to directional actions.
motivation: Choosing navigation actions depends on how informative the visual representation is. An agent that sees the target on the right of its view should prefer RotateRight, so the representation should encode where objects and regions sit in the image and relate all detected instances to each other. The authors also found that transformers trained only from sparse RL reward do not converge, so the representation must first be tied to navigation actions.
key_idea: Fuse all DETR instance features, enhanced with box/confidence/label/target cues, with ResNet-18 region features carrying 2D positional encodings in a transformer encoder–decoder, where the region descriptors act as queries. Pre-train this visual transformer by imitating shortest-path actions before A3C RL.
insight: The positional, region-query transformer representation matters more than the policy trick. VTNet without TPN (72.2 SR / 0.449 SPL) already beats ORG+TPN (69.3 / 0.394), and adding TPN helps VTNet far less than it helps ORG. Ablations (Table 2) show each part contributes: removing the global branch drops to 67.0 / 0.390, removing the decoder (plain concatenation) to 67.0 / 0.373, removing positional encoding to 71.0 / 0.432, and a single encoder over global features (VTNet_g) to 70.1 / 0.411. DETR features beat Faster R-CNN features in both ORG-style (70.1 / 0.396) and BUTD-style (70.3 / 0.387) extraction. Two components are necessary rather than helpful: without spatial enhancement of DETR features, or without IL pre-training, training fails entirely (the agent learns to stop after about 5 steps). Deeper transformers (4–6 layers) are worse than 2 layers with 4 heads.
method: Spatial-enhanced local descriptor: DETR (fine-tuned on AI2-THOR) gives 100 instance features (256-d). Each is concatenated with its normalized bbox, confidence, top semantic label and a one-hot target indicator, then fused by a 2-layer MLP with ReLU into L ∈ R^{100×256}; these serve as encoder keys/values.

Positional global descriptor: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 7×7 feature map, 1×1 conv down to 256-d, plus 2D sinusoidal positional encoding (row index on the first half of channels, column index on the second half), reshaped to G ∈ R^{49×256}.

Visual Transformer (VT): the encoder applies multi-head self-attention plus FFN over the local descriptors. The decoder uses the 49 positional region descriptors as queries attending to the encoded instances, giving a 49×256 representation. Best setting is 4 heads with 2 encoder and 2 decoder layers.

IL pre-training: the VT plus an MLP head (standing in for the LSTM, with no previous actions or states) is trained for 20 epochs with cross-entropy on Dijkstra shortest-path optimal actions, so the representation encodes directional signals.

Navigation policy: an LSTM A3C policy takes the visual representation, previous action and state. It is trained for 6M episodes with 16 asynchronous agents, reward −0.001 per step and +5 on success, using Adam at lr 1e-4 for the policy and 1e-5 for the pre-trained VT.
Optional TPN: ORG's tentative policy network for deadlock escape can be added (VTNet+TPN).

setting.backbone: DETR (fine-tuned on AI2-THOR) + ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 features + transformer encoder–decoder + LSTM A3C policy (VT and policy trained)
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR (iTHOR) 80 training rooms (20 per scene type), 22 target categories; IL pre-training on Dijkstra shortest-path action labels (20 epochs); RL for 6M episodes; DETR fine-tuned on AI2-THOR training data with augmentation
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB only (no depth, no pose, no map)
setting.action_space: discrete grid actions: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/RotateRight 45°, LookUp/LookDown 30°, Done
setting.privileged: none at test time (success requires calling Done with the target visible within 1.5 m)

numbers.extra: mean of 5 runs; L≥5 = episodes requiring at least 5 steps; model chosen by best validation SR
numbers.evidence: Table 1 'Comparison with the state-of-the-art. We report the average success rate (%) and SPL as well as their variances in parentheses by repeating experiments five times.' — VTNet 72.2 (1.0), 0.449 (0.007); L≥5: 63.4 (1.1), 0.440 (0.009)

numbers_note: Only AI2-THOR (iTHOR) is evaluated. The test set is 20 held-out rooms (40 held-out rooms split equally into val and test). SPL is printed as a fraction (e.g. 0.449) and converted to a 0-100 scale here. Values in parentheses are called 'variances' over 5 runs. The Baseline SPL differs slightly between Table 1 (0.364) and Table 2 (0.365). Other ablations (Table 2): w/o global 67.0 / 0.390, w/o decoder 67.0 / 0.373, w/o pe 71.0 / 0.432, VTNet_g 70.1 / 0.411, VTNet with Faster R-CNN† (BUTD) 70.3 / 0.387. Appendix Table 3 compares transformer depth and head counts (best: 4 heads, 2+2 layers). No numbers are given for no-pretraining or no-spatial-enhancement because training did not converge.
results: On AI2-THOR unseen test rooms, VTNet reaches 72.2% SR and 0.449 SPL (63.4% / 0.440 on L≥5 episodes). This beats the previous SOTA ORG+TPN (69.3 / 0.394), a +14.0% relative SPL gain, and ORG without TPN (65.3 / 0.375). It also beats a DETR+global concatenation baseline (62.6 / 0.364) and SAVN (40.8 / 0.161). Adding TPN raises SR to 73.5 but lowers SPL to 0.440.
limitations: No depth input: many failures are premature Done calls just beyond the 1.5 m threshold (e.g. 1.530 m, 1.572 m) because the agent misjudges distance for objects of varying size.
The transformer cannot be trained by RL alone; it needs IL pre-training with Dijkstra expert actions (privileged in training) and spatial enhancement, otherwise training fails.
Evaluated only on the small iTHOR single-room setting (120 rooms, 22 categories, grid actions) with no Habitat, continuous-action or real-robot experiments.
